result.rationale: The diff adds a fetch to Salesforce's token endpoint in the constructor that runs unconditionally (no expiry check) followed by a prisma.credential.update write, on every service instantiation. It also doesn't use refreshOAuthTokens, unlike every other adapter in this diff, so credential-sharing mode is silently skipped for Salesforce. This is verifiable, specific, introduced-by-the-diff behavior with real correctness/performance consequences (per-operation API quota use and DB writes).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a refresh-token request and `prisma.credential.update(...)` unconditionally before creating the jsforce connection (added block starting with `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)`). There is no expiry/validity check to avoid refreshing on every use. Also, unlike other adapters modified in this diff (e.g., Google/O365/Zoom/etc.), Salesforce does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper at all, so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, Salesforce will still attempt a direct refresh instead of delegating to the sync endpoint—making credential-sharing mode effectively ignored for Salesforce.
